title: Machine learning-driven optimization of lead-free CsGeBr 3  perovskite solar cells  via  charge carrier modulation and ETL engineering
content: This study aims to present a lead-free perovskite absorber to replace traditional toxic lead-based substances, aiming to improve performance while considering its production capabilities. The CsGeBr3 absorber is positioned between four distinct electron transport layers (ETLs), i.e., BaSnO3, PC60BM, CdS, and ZnSe, and a C6PcH2 hole transport layer (HTL), resulting in four unique heterojunction structures that optimize energy band alignment to enhance carrier mobility and reduce recombination. The influence of thickness and carrier concentration has been rigorously analysed in conjunction with the examination of the effects of series and shunt resistance, temperature, J–V and QE, along with the generation and recombination rates of carriers to determine the optimal efficiency. Following the final optimization, FTO/C6PcH2/CsGeBr3/BaSnO3/Au has exhibited the most favourable performance metrics, achieving VOC, JSC, FF, and PCE values of 1.56 V, 13.66 mA cm−2, 88.28%, and 18.83%, respectively. Additionally, 8 distinct supervised machine learning (ML) techniques are applied to evaluate the permutation and SHAP feature importance analysis of the materials. The final execution indicates a remarkable performance with the XGBoost algorithm (R2 = 0.995286, RMSE = 0.054404%, and MAE = 0.045593%) while achieving an accuracy of 99.73705% for PCE prediction. Overall findings indicate that Ge-based materials can effectively eliminate toxic lead, demonstrating excellent efficiency and ideal stability properties.
